<reason>PRO built a clean causal spine—speed multiplies the severity of every crash regardless of who is driving—and CON never dislodged it; CON's late claim that speed is "the variable that kills least often" contradicted the physics it had left unchallenged in its opening and PRO called that out. PRO neutralized the fines externality (both tools carry flat fines and suspension spirals; income-scaling exists in Finland/Switzerland), answered both pressure questions directly with A1/A2, and turned CON's honest "single digits, at best" concession into a damaging externality-per-benefit arithmetic that CON only met with "small and probabilistic." CON scored real points—the app-mapped-camera vs. unpredictable-patrol argument, the checkpoint trap, and the surveillance externality PRO left unanswered until closing—but CON also conceded that "neither tool survives removal," gutting its own decay argument, and its collateral-discovery route requires exactly the mass roadside encounters that constitute the motion's externality. Both sides had a clipped turn. PRO made the decision cleaner on both prongs.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's Rebuttal 2 / Closing turn on CON's "single digits" admission: reframing scaled stops as a lottery of twenty-to-fifty armed roadside encounters per dangerous driver found, versus cameras lowering kinetic energy for every driver without stopping anyone—CON's "zero hit rate" reply was memorable but left the severity-multiplier point standing.</best_rebuttal>
